The diagram above shows a unit circle and the angle $\theta $ measured in the usual way. Given that the $x$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $0.86,$ calculate the reference angle ${\theta }_{R}$ to the nearest integer.

${\theta }_{R}≈$
{{field-1}}${}^{∘}$
question.worked_solution:
The reference angle is the acute angle that $\theta $ makes with the $x$-axis.

First, we create a right-triangle by drawing a vertical line from $P$ to the $x$-axis.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14225277/assets/1b11bdb22a07da238cee479070ace299f89f186e1500ec44d9af84a7f37d12f5.png)

So, we have the following triangle, where ${\theta }_{R}$ is the reference angle of $\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14225277/assets/256deadcd68077b1cace4ec55d897c393b2ac849af0ba29748840a617c81e989.png)

We know that the hypotenuse has a length of $1$ because it is a radius of the unit circle. 

Now, using the triangle above, we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡{\theta }_{R}=\frac{0.86}{1}=0.86.
$$

Now, we compute the angle ${\theta }_{R}$ using the inverse cosine:

$$
{\theta }_{R}=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(0.86)≈{31}^{∘}
$$
